newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Sun-seeking seal takes a break in the tropics.
newsitem.headline: Sun-seeking seal takes a break in the tropics.

text.p: A sun-seeking baby seal who apparently decided to leave his frigid home for a holiday in the tropics was resting in Puerto Rico on Monday after coming ashore in the U.S. Virgin Islands last week.

The seven-month-old hooded seal, native to cooler spots like Greenland and Newfoundland, washed up on the island of St. John last Wednesday, attracting a crowd of onlookers as he rolled onto his back, clapped his flippers and hopped back into the water for a swim.

Scientists said they had no idea why the young seal had decided to swim so far south. They said they did not think it was a Caribbean Monk Seal, a species last seen in 1952 and believed to be extinct.
A hooded seal washed ashore in Puerto Rico in 1993 but there was no record that any had ever made it to the Virgin Islands before last week.

A U.S. Coast Guard helicopter transported the seal to the Caribbean Stranding Network in Puerto Rico, where it was expected to stay for about a month before being shipped to the northern United States and released.
